(i) the system can be used to store and retrieve video clips, (ii) the system can stream video clips, (iii) the system can support video operations, (iv) the system can perform similarity searches on video clips, (v) the system is scalable and (vi) the system can handle multiple queries concurrently.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new architecture and a new set of techniques for supporting continuous media applications in a DBMS.
the development of new techniques and algorithms for the storage, indexing, searching, retrieval, and transmission of video data in the context of distributed databases.
the development of a system that supports the storage, retrieval, and streaming of video data.

our system is a distributed database server that supports continuous media.
our system provides a new and innovative approach to video data management.
we are developing an integrated system to handle multimedia data in a distributed environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the infrastructure to support a video database management system.
we have developed a system for managing video data that is based on a well-defined data model and is able to handle video data efficiently and effectively.
we are building a distributed video server for continuous media that supports a rich set of video operations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the traditional database systems are well-suited for the video data management, provided the system components are modified appropriately.
video is a well-defined data model that has its own description, attributes, and applicable methods, which can be used to build a new class of applications that can handle video data.
video data is best treated as an integral component of a database system rather than a separate entity.
